topic.readerProblem: An SEO team asked to take on AEO/GEO needs to know which of its existing work still applies, what is genuinely new, what to stop doing, and in what order to act.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity name a brand; this page turns that measurement problem into a transition plan for SEO teams, using AEOeye's crawler access study and its own page-consolidation history as first-hand evidence.

assessment: The page splits an SEO team's work into what carries over (crawl access, trust and indexing, per Google's AI-features documentation and AEOeye's 384-site crawler access study), what is new (prompt-level sampling, third-party corroboration, quotable passages, per-engine testing) and what to stop, then gives an ordered plan and a leadership reporting frame. It rests on vendor documentation, two arXiv papers, Pew and SparkToro data and AEOeye's own artifacts. It deliberately does not claim that GEO edits raise rankings or citations in production, that schema or llms.txt moves citations, that AI answers name only two or three brands, or any per-engine ranking of recommendation rates.

sources.supports: Last updated December 2025: SEO best practices remain relevant to AI Overviews and AI Mode; a page must be indexed and snippet-eligible to be a supporting link, with no additional requirements; crawling must be allowed in robots.txt and by any CDN; no new machine-readable files, AI text files, markup or special schema.org data are needed; query fan-out; AI-feature traffic is reported inside the Web search type of Search Console.
Of the E-E-A-T aspects, 'trust is most important' (page last updated 2026-10-01).
A redirect is a strong signal that its target should become canonical, and canonicalization helps search engines consolidate signals such as links into a single preferred URL.
Wikipedia defines generative engine optimization as also known as answer engine optimization (AEO): the practice of improving visibility in responses generated by generative AI systems.
Pew browsing data from 900 US adults, March 2025: a traditional result was clicked in 8% of visits with an AI summary versus 15% without; a link inside the summary was clicked in 1% of visits.

SparkToro with Gumshoe.ai, November-December 2025: 600 volunteers, 2,961 runs; under a 1 in 100 chance that two responses from ChatGPT or Google's AI list the same brands; the authors call visibility percentage across dozens to hundreds of prompts run multiple times a reasonable metric.

Microsoft announced the AI Performance report in public preview (February 2026) showing citation counts for Copilot, AI summaries in Bing and select partner integrations, with a sample of grounding queries.

Chen et al. (September 2025 preprint; data August-September 2025): AI search favours earned media over brand-owned and social sources; US software-product prompts 72.7% earned for search-enabled GPT-4o versus 45.4% in Google; top-five domain overlap with Google 15-33% in product categories; consumer electronics Claude about 93.7% and GPT about 93.6% earned versus Perplexity about 53.3% earned, 31.6% brand, 15.1% social.

Aggarwal et al., GEO (KDD 2024): generative engines retrieve sources and write from them; adding statistics, quotations or cited sources gave a 30-40% relative gain on Position-Adjusted Word Count in the authors' own engine; keyword stuffing did not help; effects on search rankings were not evaluated.

OAI-SearchBot is used to surface sites in ChatGPT search; sites that opt out of OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers though they can still appear as navigational links; each bot setting is independent.
PerplexityBot is designed to surface and link websites in Perplexity search results and is not used to crawl content for AI foundation models; confirms the bot name used in the access checklist.
Claude-SearchBot navigates the web to improve search result quality; blocking it may reduce a site's visibility in user search results; confirms the bot name used in the access checklist.
